title: Identity, divine agency and scarcity: evidence and scenario notebook
scope: A companion to three expanded main articles. A historical hypothesis, an interpretation of attributed sayings, an observed price index, an institutional forecast and a new conditional scenario are different record types. No automatic monitoring or completed 2027 outcome assessment is implied.

articles.title: Divine will, distinct agency and inward formation
AI representation, scarcity and conditional access

evidence.title: One earlier individual, not merely influence
evidence.record: The strong model identifies the earlier Teacher and the historical origin of Jesus with one individual, with later biographical relocation and community transmission.
evidence.implication: Keep identity, direct transmission, shared milieu and a composite portrait as distinct alternatives. Similarity alone does not decide between them.
evidence.limits: The working name makes the proposal independently inspectable. It does not establish that no evidence could refute it or that it already outranks other explanations.

evidence.title: What can actually be assigned to the Teacher?
evidence.record: Schiffman's discussion distinguishes passages mentioning the Teacher from the whole Qumran library and allows the possibility of a succession of leaders under the designation.
evidence.implication: Build the comparison from attributable roles and sayings, rather than treating all scrolls as one person's work.
evidence.limits: This is a consulted scholarly discussion, not a fresh collation of Hebrew manuscripts or a settled identification of the Teacher.

evidence.title: Kinship and living witnesses
evidence.record: Galatians 1:18-19, 1 Corinthians 9:5 and 15:3-8 preserve kinship, named leaders and surviving witnesses within Paul's account.
evidence.implication: An earlier community can survive across generations, but namesake succession and later visionary appearances are additional propositions requiring their own evidence.
evidence.limits: The letters do not provide a complete absolute chronology. Their positive constraints are not erased by that absence.

evidence.title: James, Pilate and Tiberius
evidence.record: Josephus, Antiquities 20.200, relates James to Jesus called Christ in a first-century administrative sequence. Tacitus, Annals 15.44, places Christus's execution under Tiberius and Pilate.
evidence.implication: A relocation hypothesis needs a particular account of how the chronology arose and what source evidence supports that account.
evidence.limits: Neither is an eyewitness biography of Jesus. A later source is not thereby false, and a Roman author is not proof of independent consultation of an execution file.

evidence.title: A distinct will and limited knowledge
evidence.record: Mark 14:32-36 depicts anguish and a will placed under the Father's; Mark 13:32 distinguishes the Son's knowledge from the Father's; John 5:30 describes seeking the sender's will.
evidence.implication: These texts support study of obedient agency without requiring the claim that the subject has no will of his own.
evidence.limits: The narrative does not supply direct access to every belief of the historical Jesus or a measurement of his neural activity.

evidence.title: Exalted portrayal and dependence coexist
evidence.record: John 8:58, 10:30, 17:5 and Thomas's address in 20:28 supply high divine portrayals, while John 17:3 and 20:17 distinguish the Father and sender. Philippians 2 joins exalted language with obedience.
evidence.implication: Distinguish Jesus's attributed words, narration, other speakers and later interpretation. The ethical account of submission does not require deleting the high-Christology passages.
evidence.limits: These observations do not settle the historical authenticity of each saying or impose one later theological reconciliation.

evidence.title: Two levels of correction
evidence.record: The article proposes that an inward moral model can correct an impulse, while testimony and reflection can in turn correct the person's interpretation of that model.
evidence.implication: A model of God describes the human representation without deciding whether its divine referent is real. Conviction and felt presence do not by themselves certify the model's truth.
evidence.limits: Higher and lower are value-ordering terms, not anatomical locations; vibration here is experiential language, not an established physical measurement.

evidence.title: An interruptible system is not automatically a centralized political switch
evidence.record: The superintelligence statement advocates a conditional development prohibition. EU AI Act Article 14 specifies human oversight, override and interruption of high-risk systems.
evidence.implication: Investigate who controls development and deployment, which exceptions apply and how affected parties can challenge decisions.
evidence.limits: An advocacy statement is not an enacted worldwide ban. A human stop mechanism can be a safeguard rather than a coercive instrument; actual implementation must decide the comparison.

evidence.title: Digital currency is not a single uniform control mechanism
evidence.record: The January 23, 2025 US executive order opposes federal CBDC development; the ECB's digital-euro FAQ distinguishes conditional payments from programmable spending restrictions.
evidence.implication: Follow actual identity, payment and delivery controls rather than assuming a CBDC is required for exclusion or always designed to implement it.
evidence.limits: These are official positions and design commitments, not a comprehensive audit of deployed or future systems.

evidence.title: Fuel priority and cards in Russia
evidence.record: Reuters' July 15, 2026 report describes priority fuel for food-delivery vehicles and a government fuel-card mechanism.
evidence.implication: This supplies a specific scarcity-to-allocation observation to investigate through actual rules, places, issuers and recipients.
evidence.limits: It does not establish one nationwide card-only retail rule or a political-allegiance condition for all purchasers.

evidence.title: August 2026 international food-price baseline
evidence.record: FAO's September 4 release reports an August index of 133.3, up 1.9% on the revised preceding month and 2.5% year on year, but 16.8% below March 2022.
evidence.implication: Record the release vintage and compare the same series with subsequent releases.
evidence.limits: Internationally traded commodity prices are not local household bills, wage-adjusted food access or a declaration of famine. The live page can later change.

evidence.title: Recovery is part of the September 2026 energy baseline
evidence.record: EIA's September outlook forecasts Brent averaging about $74 per barrel in 2027 versus $91 in 2026, with most Middle Eastern production and trade recovering toward pre-conflict averages by the second quarter of 2027.
evidence.implication: Compare a recovery pathway with prolonged disruption instead of presenting deterioration as the only forecast.
evidence.limits: The forecast was completed September 3 and released September 9. The projected prices and recovery have not been observed in 2027; some producers remain constrained in the baseline.

evidence.title: Fertilizer and later agricultural exposure
evidence.record: The World Bank's April 2026 outlook projected fertilizer prices rising 31% in 2026 and warned of later production effects, under stated assumptions about easing disruption.
evidence.implication: A lagged agricultural mechanism should be evaluated at the planting and harvest cycle of the affected place.
evidence.limits: A 2026 price forecast is not an observed global harvest loss or proof of worldwide famine in 2027.

evidence.title: Climate and trade-route risks into early 2027
evidence.record: The IRC's September 18, 2026 release warns of interacting climate and conflict pressures into late 2026 and early 2027. IPC's framework separates household Catastrophe from area-level Famine.
evidence.implication: Track food gaps, malnutrition, mortality, displacement and relief access in named populations, not only world price indexes.
evidence.limits: The warning is not a confirmed future outcome. The Wiki has not independently run the climate models or performed an IPC classification.

scenarios.geography: Gulf production and international oil trade
scenarios.trigger: Production, transport or refining disruption continues beyond the recovery interval assumed in the September EIA baseline.
scenarios.conditional_projection: Persistent disruption would weaken the recovery pathway and can prolong energy-price and distribution pressure.
scenarios.measure: Monthly production and export volumes, route availability, inventories, Brent and local diesel prices recorded separately.
scenarios.alternative: Sustained route reopening, restored output and lower prices would support recovery rather than continued escalation.

scenarios.geography: Named fuel- or fertilizer-import-dependent farming regions, fixed before assessment
scenarios.trigger: Farmers face input disruption during an identified planting or cultivation period.
scenarios.conditional_projection: Reduced or delayed input use may affect the next harvest or increase costs, with effects mediated by weather, reserves and substitution.
scenarios.measure: Input availability and use, planted area, crop yields, import volumes and the relevant seasonal calendar.
scenarios.alternative: Substitute inputs, assistance, adequate weather, imports or restored supplies can prevent the proposed output loss.

scenarios.geography: Each documented fuel or food allocation jurisdiction, not all Russia or the world
scenarios.trigger: A verified shortage leads to an actual mandatory allocation order or extends an existing one.
scenarios.conditional_projection: Access may become dependent on a credential as well as money; extension to further goods or conditions must be documented separately.
scenarios.measure: Issuer, order text, commodity, eligible population, refusals, appeals, exemptions, effective and expiry dates.
scenarios.alternative: Open need-based eligibility, an effective sunset and restored ordinary sales would not support a claim of expanding permanent control.

scenarios.geography: Named households and markets with comparable income and price data
scenarios.trigger: Essential-food or fuel prices increase while real income or employment falls.
scenarios.conditional_projection: The working time or income share required for necessities may rise even while some property or business assets decline in price.
scenarios.measure: A fixed local basic-diet basket, wages, employment, transport costs, debt service and relevant asset prices as distinct series.
scenarios.alternative: Rising wages, transfers, lower essential prices or improved employment can relieve the squeeze. Deflation is not defined as cash becoming worthless.

scenarios.geography: Individually identified deployments of automated eligibility or transaction systems
scenarios.trigger: A public or private institution delegates a consequential access decision to an automated system.
scenarios.conditional_projection: Opaque rules and ineffective appeals could extend exclusion; a speaking interface alone does not establish such power.
scenarios.measure: Legal authority, system role, human override, reason-giving, appeal outcomes, error correction and consequences for affected people.
scenarios.alternative: Contestable decisions, effective correction and reduced exclusion would count against an unqualified coercive-control projection.

scenarios.geography: IPC-assessed or comparably monitored crisis populations, named before outcome review
scenarios.trigger: Conflict, weather, livelihood losses and reduced assistance jointly impair food access.
scenarios.conditional_projection: Severe local food insecurity may worsen without implying a uniform worldwide famine or depression.
scenarios.measure: Household food-consumption gaps, acute malnutrition, mortality, displacement, market function and humanitarian access.
scenarios.alternative: Improved security, transfers, market supply and aid can interrupt the trajectory. A price spike alone does not meet all famine criteria.

forecast_rules: Review dates organize future research, not dates extracted from Revelation or deadlines retroactively assigned to earlier predictions. No outcomes or probabilities have been assigned. Later observations must retain their own dates, geographic scope and source versions.
earlier_material: Original forecast ledgers, source conversations, the 148-passage concordance, social-media snapshots and the awaiting-export scarcity report remain unchanged.
